newsitem.title: USA: U.S. man called "predator" says he killed another.
newsitem.headline: U.S. man called "predator" says he killed another.

text.p: A Florida man who has been legally labeled a "sexual predator" and who is in prison for killing two young sisters has confessed to another murder and a sexual assault, police said Tuesday.

Howard Ault, 30, already in the Broward County Jail for the kidnapping and murder of two young sisters, confessed to sex crimes and murders he has been charged with and told reporters of additional assaults and killings he said he had gotten away with, police said.

The Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel reported Tuesday that Ault told its reporter he had assaulted a female neighbour and a female friend, and told how he had picked up a woman at a Fort Lauderdale strip club, killed her and dumped her body in the Florida Everglades in 1992.
A police spokeswoman said Fort Lauderdale police were investigating those statements.
Ault told the newspaper he chose to talk to the reporter to clear his conscience and to let the public know that people with urges like his should be watched closely.
"I don't feel that what's wrong with me can be repaired," Ault said. "...Anybody that has the problem that I have, they don't need to be on the street."

Ault was arrested in November and charged with the kidnapping and murder of two sisters, Alicia Sybilla Jones, 7, and DeAnn Emerald Mu-min, 11, of Oakland Park, Florida, whose bodies were found in the attic of his home. He also was charged with sexually assaulting the older girl.

Labeled a "sexual predator" by the legal system, Ault was previously accused by another 11-year-old girl of accusing her on Dec. 31, 1995, but he was not arrested on that charge until last autumn, after the two sisters were killed, although he was under house arrest for still another attack on a young girl when he was arrested.
One of the officers involved in the alleged Dec. 31, 1995, attack was fired and another was suspended and demoted in January for failing to arrest Ault in a timely matter.
